explanations.explanation: A colt, friend. Jesus says they'll find one tied there as soon as they enter the village (Mark 11:2). He gives the whole plan before they take a single step. I'd have forgotten what I was sent for by the second street.
A camel would be a LOT of animal, friend. Jesus says they'll find a colt tied there (Mark 11:2). That's the one on the errand list. A camel on this errand would be quite the surprise.

A ram is a fair guess, but Jesus doesn't name one. He says they'll find a colt tied there as soon as they enter the village (Mark 11:2). He says exactly what they'll find, and that colt is the whole errand.
True, friend. Jesus says it's a colt "on which no one has ever sat" (Mark 11:2). That's a detail He gives right up front. Nobody had ridden this colt yet.
Not quite, baker. Jesus says the colt is one "on which no one has ever sat" (Mark 11:2). So this is a colt nobody has ridden yet. It's right there in His instructions.

explanations.answer: The Lord needs it and will return it shortly
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus tells them to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) Short, clear, and it even says the colt is coming back. I wish my instructions came that tidy. Mine usually end with "you'll figure it out."

explanations.answer: The Teacher will pay you back for it tonight
explanations.explanation: Close on the "giving it back" part, but that's not the line. Jesus tells them to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) Nothing about paying anybody back tonight. The words He hands them are the words they use.

explanations.answer: The priests have sent us here to collect it
explanations.explanation: No priests in this errand, friend. Jesus tells the two disciples to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) The words come from Jesus, and they're short enough to remember while your heart is pounding.

Not this time, baker. The text says the disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, "and the people gave them permission" (Mark 11:6). Nobody blocks the way. Jesus handed them the right words, and they worked.

False is right, friend. The disciples answer as Jesus instructed, and "the people gave them permission." (Mark 11:6) No standoff, no arguing. I bet those two let out a breath they'd been holding the whole walk.

True, baker. The disciples lead the colt to Jesus, throw their cloaks over it, "and He sat on it." (Mark 11:7) The colt nobody had ridden before now has Jesus on it. The errand worked out just as He said.
Not false, friend. The text says they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, "and He sat on it." (Mark 11:7) That's the whole reason for the errand. Jesus rides the colt.
Branches, baker! Others in the crowd spread "branches they had cut from the fields" (Mark 11:8). Some gave their cloaks and some gave branches. Everybody brought what they had.

Grain sounds like a field thing, I'll give you that. But the text says the crowd spread "branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) The fields are right, and the branches are what got cut. Grain didn't make the road.
Straw is a good field guess, friend. But Mark says others spread "branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) So the road got cloaks and branches. No straw in this crowd.

David, baker! The crowd shouts, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) David was Israel's king, and the crowd calls him "our father." The people ahead and behind are all shouting about Jesus.
Abraham is a big name, friend, and he was the father of Israel's people. But the crowd shouts, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) The kingdom they name is David's.

Jacob is a good guess, baker, but he's not the name in this shout. The crowd cries, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) David was Israel's king, and it's his kingdom they bless.
True, baker. Jesus entered Jerusalem "and went into the temple courts." (Mark 11:11) After all that shouting, He walks straight in. Quiet after the noise.
Not false, friend. Mark says Jesus entered Jerusalem "and went into the temple courts." (Mark 11:11) The crowd was LOUD, and then He goes right in. That's where the next part happens.

explanations.answer: Goes out to Bethany with the Twelve
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Since it was already late, Jesus "went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) The Twelve are His closest disciples. He looks at everything, then heads out for the night. And the story isn't over yet.

explanations.answer: Stays the night in the temple courts
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says that since it was already late, Jesus "went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) The Twelve are His closest disciples. He doesn't stay in the temple courts, and the story isn't over yet.

explanations.answer: Heads back to Jericho with the crowd
explanations.explanation: Jericho is behind them, baker. Mark says that since it was already late, Jesus "went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) The Twelve are His closest disciples. No crowd goes with them, and the story isn't over yet.
